claim.pdf_says: p1093 ends at 'g)  a REWRITE statement with the FROM phrase'. p1094 opens with three further list items, each set as its own labelled item: 'h)  the data item referenced in the DESTINATION clause of an element of the operand of a VALIDATE statement' / 'i)  the subject of a data description entry that contains a VALIDATE-STATUS clause that references the element of the operand of a VALIDATE statement' / 'j)  a WRITE statement with the FROM phrase.'
claim.markdown_says: g) a REWRITE statement with the FROM phrase h) the data item referenced in the DESTINATION clause of an element of the operand of a VALIDATE statement i) the subject of a data description entry that contains a VALIDATE-STATUS clause that references the element of the operand of a VALIDATE statement j) a WRITE statement with the FROM phrase.
claim.why_it_matters: Items h), i) and j) of the list in D.8.3 (permitted receiving-operand contexts for a strongly-typed group item) have lost their list structure entirely: all three are run into the body of item g) as inline text, on the wrong side of the page-1094 anchor. The text is preserved verbatim but the enumeration is destroyed, so a reader or tool parsing 'the contexts a) through g)' silently gets the wrong list, and none of h), i), j) can be cited by label.

verdict.reasoning: Both sources were re-rendered and read independently. The claim's two factual observations are accurate: PDF p1093 (printed folio 1063) does end its list at 'g) a REWRITE statement with the FROM phrase', and PDF p1094 (folio 1064) opens with h), i) and j) each set as its own hanging-indent item at the same level as a)-g); markdown specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 43887 does run all four onto a single line. But the delta between the two is nothing but the three inter-item line breaks, and that is exactly the page-break / whitespace formatting class this verification is instructed to reject. Four points refute the finding as stated. (1) NOTHING IS LOST. Every word of h), i) and j) is present verbatim and in the correct order, and so are the literal labels 'h)', 'i)' and 'j)' -- the claim itself concedes the text is verbatim. The only characters absent are newlines. (2) THE STATED HARM IS FALSE. The claim asserts 'none of h), i), j) can be cited by label'. All three are directly greppable in the markdown by their label: 'h) the data item referenced in the DESTINATION clause', 'i) the subject of a data description entry that contains a VALIDATE-STATUS', and 'j) a WRITE statement with the FROM phrase.' each match. A reader sees the labels plainly on the same line; nothing is silent. (3) THERE IS NO LIST MARKUP TO DESTROY. This transcription never uses markdown list syntax for lettered items anywhere -- siblings a) through f) at lines 43875-43885 are plain paragraph lines with a three-space indent and a literal 'a) ' text prefix, identical in kind to the run-together line. So the claim that the items 'lost their list structure entirely' overstates a lost newline as lost semantic markup; the enumeration labels, which are the only structure the transcription ever encoded, all survive. (4) THE ANCHOR PLACEMENT IS THE DOCUMENTED CONVENTION, NOT AN ERROR. The transcription attributes a page-straddling paragraph to the page where it STARTS: PDF p1093's own top-of-page continuation ('group items, are restricted to those that don't affect the integrity...') is likewise absent from page-1093.md because it belongs to a paragraph beginning on p1092. Given the extractor merged g)-j) into one paragraph starting on p1093, filing it under the page-1093 anchor follows that convention; 'on the wrong side of the page-1094 anchor' is page-break furniture, an explicit reject criterion. A document-wide scan found only 7 lines that begin with a lettered label and contain more than one, and several of those (lines 11339, 19674, 23660) are genuine inline 'a) X, or b) Y' enumerations that the PDF itself sets inline -- so line 43887 is a rare cosmetic blemish worth a cleanup pass, but it changes no content, no ordering, no label and no meaning, and no rule of D.8.3 can be misread because of it.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The complete difference is three missing line breaks at the p1093/p1094 boundary: items g), h), i) and j) of the D.8.3 receiving-operand list are concatenated onto markdown line 43887 instead of occupying four lines. All text, all four labels, and the item order are preserved character-for-character, every label remains individually citable and greppable, and the transcription encodes lettered items as literal text prefixes rather than markdown lists everywhere, so no markup was lost. Downgrade from 'structural' to a cosmetic line-break/whitespace nit if the ledger tracks such items at all.
